narr: On September 6th, a cold front entered into West Virginia and stirred up showers and thunderstorms for the afternoon. One storm in particular that passed through Fayette County was strong enough to cause two trees and power lines to be blown down. The severe threat quickly diminished as drier air filtered in behind the frontal passage.||Another weak cold front arrived two days later on the 8th, this time imposing a flash flooding threat. Despite the front having already crossed much of West Virginia by the afternoon, there was still enough lift along the foothills and mountains that promoted slow moving showers and storms. Enough rain fell in McDowell County that resulted in high water along a local road for a few hours.
ev: High water was observed along Jenkinsjones Mountain Road.
lsr: High water on Jenkinjones Mountain Road.
